intent: Teach continuation_lines() that the element lines and closing paren of a multi-line array literal are not statements. This is defect (a) in docs/kcov-under-report.md, in the fourth flavour found this session, and it caps arch_perf_fixes.sh plus at least two of the libs still to be tested.
scope: meta/scripts/lib/shell_coverage_lines.py (one regex, one helper, and array state in the main loop)
python_pkg/tests/test_shell_coverage_lines.py (four new cases: one positive, three negative)
Non-goal: the backslash-continued ASSIGNMENT flavour that caps bt_adapter.sh line 97, still deferred
meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt (arch_perf_fixes.sh removed, since the fix takes it to 100%)
changes: Added _ARRAY_OPEN, matching an assignment whose value opens a multi-line array literal -- `local -a c=(`, `declare -A m=(`, `FILES=(`, `x+=(` -- with nothing but an optional comment after the paren. While open, every line is excluded until a `)` that is not itself inside quotes.
Added _closes_array(), which finds that closing paren by recomputing quote state from the start of the line for each candidate, so an element like "a(b)" does not end the literal early.
The rule is symmetric with the existing multi-line-quote case: bash reports the WHOLE assignment at its OPENING line, so that line stays a statement and everything up to the closing paren is data.

Added four tests: a multi-line array marks its elements and closing paren; a single-line `x=(a b)` does NOT; an element containing a parenthesis does not close the literal early; and `x=$(echo hi)` is a command substitution rather than an array literal.
Removed linux_configuration/scripts/single_use/fixes/lib/arch_perf_fixes.sh from meta/shell-coverage-allowlist.txt: the fix takes it to 100.00%, so it now meets the bar.

verification.command: PS4='+L${LINENO} ' bash -x on a minimal multi-line array literal
verification.evidence: bash prints '+L3 items=(\'one\' \'two\')' for an array opened on line 3 and closed on line 6, and never emits lines 4, 5 or 6. The elements and closing paren are data; only the opening line is a statement.
22 passed. shell_coverage_lines.py: 71 statements, 48 branches, 0 missed, 0 partial = 100%, so both arms of every new branch are covered as the repo's fail_under=100 branch gate requires.

verification.command: Diff old vs new predicate over every allowlisted lib plus the six already cleared, printing each newly excluded line WITH its text
verification.evidence: 91 newly excluded lines across 10 libs, and every one is an array element or a closing paren: common.sh's tool tables, packages.sh's associative arrays, arch_sysctl.sh's sysctl key/value maps, thorium_repairs.sh's four path lists, ubuntu_perf_fixes.sh's sssd unit list, clean_audio_filters.sh's model search paths, trace_prefix.sh, trace_stubs.sh and arch_perf_fixes.sh's candidate list. No ordinary statement was caught -- the fail-open direction this module's test header warns about.

verification.command: Re-measure seven libs through fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh after the change
verification.evidence: arch_perf_fixes.sh 93.48% -> 100.00% (43/43). bt_audio.sh 127/127, arch_perf_report.sh 59/59, arch_perf_probes.sh 93/93, ubuntu_perf_more.sh 32/32, bt_report.sh 37/37 and bt_pairing.sh 65/65 all unchanged at 100.00%. One gained, six held, none went DOWN.

verification.command: The handoff's acceptance test: dot_resolver_install.sh and rpi_nc_ca.sh through features/lib/tests/run_all.sh with its jail_args
verification.evidence: dot_resolver_install.sh: 39/39 = 100.00% and rpi_nc_ca.sh: 73/73 = 100.00%, exactly the figures the handoff names as the instrument's acceptance criteria.
'check_shell_coverage.sh: every checked shell library meets the coverage bar', exit 0, with the allowlist line already removed so the lib had no exemption.

risks: This is the second denominator change of the session, so the same arithmetic bound applies: _measure computes covered_set = (executed|traced) & denominator, so a lib already at 100.00% cannot regress from excluding more lines. The six cleared libs were re-measured anyway and all held.

_ARRAY_OPEN deliberately requires the line to END at the open paren. `x=(a` followed by more elements on later lines would not match, and neither would a `for x in (` construct, which is not valid bash anyway. Narrower than necessary is the safe direction here, since over-detection inflates coverage.
rollback: git revert the commit; continuation_lines() loses array tracking and the four new tests go with it.

After rollback, re-measure arch_perf_fixes.sh and expect it back at 93.48%. It is not on the cleared list at that point, so no gate breaks -- but if the follow-up clearing commit has landed, revert that too.
